speaker: The Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance, and the Minister for National Development)
text: I seek your permission to answer these three Parliamentary Questions together, as well as the other Parliamentary Questions on this topic, namely, Question Nos 3 and 45 for written answer today; and Parliamentary Questions filed by Mr Gerald Giam1,2, Ms Hany Soh3, Ms Joan Pereira4, Mr Sharael Taha5,6, Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong, Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui7 and Mr Gan Thiam Poh8 scheduled for subsequent Sittings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance, and the Minister for National Development)
text: Members who filed these Parliamentary Questions for subsequent Sittings may wish to withdraw their respective Parliamentary Questions if their queries are sufficiently addressed today.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The decision to close STC was not an easy decision, nor was it made lightly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Given Singapore's small size and land constraints, the Government continually reviews our land use plans to meet present and future needs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: At the same time, local horse racing has also experienced declining spectatorship over the years.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In developing our long-term land use strategies and plans, the Government has actively engaged the public to understand their needs and aspirations.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These engagements have strongly affirmed that we need more land for housing, as well as a diversity of spaces for leisure and recreation, to provide a quality living environment for Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked whether the use of the Singapore Racecourse site under the current Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) Master Plan has been revised to include housing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: At the Committee of Supply debate earlier this year, the Ministry of National Development announced that we have started on our Draft Master Plan review, which will take place over the next two to three years.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Government intends to update the revised land use for the site to include housing in the upcoming Master Plan.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Hany Soh and Mr Louis Chua asked about the redevelopment plans for the site.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The site will be holistically developed to meet the increasing demand for housing, including public housing, as well as leisure and recreation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is part of a larger overall plan for the North Region.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: URA will consider how the site can be developed: (a) to create a distinct identity for the precinct, taking into account its unique characteristics; and (b) to build on the green character of our North Region and the site's proximity to major parks and nature areas, such as the Sungei Buloh Wetlands Reserve, Mandai Mangroves and Mudflats, Lim Chu Kang Agri-Food cluster and the Mandai Wildlife Reserve attractions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Government is studying the potential uses for the site, including the number of dwelling units that can be injected.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Details of the redevelopment plan will be made known once the relevant studies and assessments are completed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We made the announcement now to give trainers and owners sufficient time to make the necessary arrangements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This also allows them to have several more races, culminating in the Singapore Gold Cup in October 2024.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Hany Soh, Mr Gerald Giam, Mr Sharael Taha and Mr Edward Chia have asked what assistance will be given to workers affected by the cessation of horse racing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will make every effort to assist and ease the transition for them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There are two different groups of workers affected – those employed by STC and those employed by the trainers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The STC employees will continue to be employed for at least the next 15 months up till October 2024, with some staying until closure in 2027.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Upon cessation of their employment, they will receive retrenchment packages in line with Ministry of Manpower guidelines.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In addition, they will receive job placement assistance, career guidance, skills training and counselling so that they can find new jobs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) has also stepped in to offer support.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The horse trainers employ or engage about another 420 workers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: While these are not STC employees, STC will nevertheless lean forward to work with their employers, the trainers, to provide support to these workers and ease their transition.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The media had recently reported that some equestrian entities are prepared to offer them jobs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: STC will also be extending employment facilitation, skills training and career counselling.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Members have also asked what will happen to the racehorses.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They will have to be rehomed once the races cease.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the meantime, STC has already rolled out support for racehorse owners and trainers for horse maintenance, as well as horse exportation and placement.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: STC is discussing with owners and trainers what additional support they may need to rehome their horses and will do its best to meet reasonable requests.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Some trainers have highlighted concerns that the owners might abandon their horses.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I hope that this is indeed not the case and I would caution any owner against so doing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Owners have the responsibility to look after their horses.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It would be an offence under the Animals and Birds Act to abandon their horses or fail to care appropriately for them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: STC is committed to working with owners to manage their horses in a responsible manner, such as through rehoming, either overseas or in a stable in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Members have also asked about the impact of the closure of STC on equestrian activities in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: While horse racing will cease, other equestrian activities are not affected by STC's closure.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Sport Singapore engages regularly with the Equestrian Federation of Singapore which oversees our national team's training.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The STC's closure does not affect our national equestrian team's training, which is located at Jalan Mashhor.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On heritage, we recognise the rich history of the Turf Club and the racing community.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many of my Woodgrove residents are very happy and look forward to the redevelopment of the Kranji Turf Club into more housing and recreational facilities, especially for the young couples.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But at the same time, some have given me feedback that they are also rather concerned in terms of the traffic congestion situation that is already happening around that area because of our close proximity to the Checkpoint and also to the various highways.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I am just wondering, for the purposes of this redevelopment, would we be working very closely with the Ministry of Transport (MOT) to ensure that we will look into the additional populations that are coming in, at the same time, addressing the concerns of the traffic congestion there?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The second supplementary question that I have is that many of my residents have shared with me that they appreciate the many fond memories that they have seen in the culture and events that have happened at STC.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: All of these things will be part of the assessments and technical studies that have to be done as part of the land use review and site preparation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With regard to the second question about whether, when it is redeveloped, regard will be had to the heritage, the answer is yes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We are very mindful of the identity and heritage of various areas.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the early years when we were doing our redevelopment, we used to clear a lot of things and it was just new buildings coming up.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But increasingly, we have become much more sensitive – not only as a Ministry, but as a population – to our history and heritage.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This was very evident when we did the long-term plan review, and that is one of the pillars that has come out of the long-term plan review.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have said that we will do that for the old Police Academy site, also for Paya Lebar.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Similarly, for this site, we will have regard to the heritage.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The Minister said that other equestrian sports will not be affected.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Is there currently any scheme to use retired racehorses for other equestrian sports?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If so, would this supply of horses not be constrained after the Singapore racecourse closes down, leading to higher costs for buying and importing horses for equestrian sports?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the question of retired racehorses going to other equestrian sports, that may have to be directed to the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth in terms of sports.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But I just want to clarify something about these horses.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These are racehorses and the majority of them would probably continue racing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the question is how to get them to places where they can continue to race.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, exportation would be one of the main strategies to deal with these horses.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In fact, the exportation of horses does take place quite regularly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I understand from STC that every month, there are actually a few.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think some interest has been expressed in Malaysia in taking in some of the racehorses from STC when it closes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But obviously, this is a conversation that we are having with the owners to see what they would like to do with the horses.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But bottom line, we will find homes for all the horses.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With respect to the announcement of STC dated 5 June 2023, whether all relevant stakeholders have been consulted in the decision-making process and, if not, why was it not undertaken in arriving at this decision?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On consultation, there are different types of consultation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With respect to the decision on land use, what the site should be used for, this is no different from decisions that we make in respect of other sites that are developed for public or other housing, and that is a decision that the Government has to take.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We would not usually go for public consultation on whether or not to take back a particular site.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That has to be part of the planning that the Government looks at.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But before the decision was made, we had engaged very widely with Singaporeans at large on land use and this was under the long-term plan review as well as other regular engagements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And one thing which came back very strongly – not just from Singaporeans whom we engaged, but in this House in recent debates – was the need for more housing, in particular, public housing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, that was one of the imperatives and drivers as we looked at and reviewed the amount of land available for housing and that informed our decision as to whether to take back this site for housing purposes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the decision, having been made, what is very important is that all the stakeholders who are affected by the decision need to be assisted with the transition and that includes, as I mentioned earlier, the employees of STC, the trainers, the horse owners, the employees of the trainers, and there are some tenants, for example, on the site.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Those tenants, for tenancies like food and beverage and so on, the contractual arrangements with them will be fulfilled and, if there are one or two who may need to be relocated, we will assist with the relocation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With regard to the duration of 15 months, let me explain how that is derived.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And horse exportation does not happen just so easily – you need time for quarantine, you need time for vaccination, you need time for transport, you need time to have them rehomed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, working backwards, it was determined that October next year should be the last race, which means that between now and October, these employees, all of them, whether STC or for the trainers, will be able to continue in employment.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then the question is when it stops, because once the last race finishes, in a sense, especially for the trainers, there are no further races.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, there will still be horses to be looked after for exportation, but you would not be preparing for racing, for example.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the workload is already going to start tapering off.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, there is still a period between 2024 and 2026 when there will be a tailing off.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, this is something that STC, as well as the trainers, will have to work through with their employees to bring the employment to an end.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For STC, as I mentioned earlier, some will have to continue being employed right up to 2027, because the administration staff, whoever is doing payroll, payments and so on, they will still need to be around to do the winding down.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The second point that Mr Patrick Tay raised was those employees who may be experiencing hardship and may require extra support.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I would certainly encourage them to raise with their employers and with STC if they have special needs, or face particular hardship, and we will lean forward to assist them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The third point on whether STC could allow workers to undertake skills training for other jobs, the answer is definitely yes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But I think the real question is: we need to be sensitive to what the workers themselves would like to do.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There may be some who are able to find other jobs in the equestrian industry and, if they are able to find them those jobs and they want to continue, that should be very much their choice.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But there may be some who may decide to exit the industry and wish to enter a new industry.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For those, we would most certainly make every effort to assist them to be reskilled.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The first is, in relation to the existing Kranji Turf Club as well as the former site of the Turf Club at Bukit Timah, what is the targeted completion date of the first batch of residential properties to be completed over there?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Hence, the second supplementary question is: can there be provisions to extend the closure of the Kranji Turf Club should there be delays in other processes?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For the Kranji Turf Club, this is something that has been earmarked for immediate development.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, if you have an extension, it is going to push back the plans to be able to develop the area immediately.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Given the shortage in housing, if you push back and you extend it, it is going to push back the housing programme for the houses that can be built in the Kranji area.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the question is: extend for what purpose?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, if it is extended just to have more races, although it may not seem so, but that would not really help, in the sense that—consider this: the announcement has already been made.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You already know that the operations are going to come to an end with respect to racing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, let me just run through for Bukit Timah because Bukit Timah, when it was taken back, primarily at that time, the reasons why it was taken back was twofold.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I am not sure whether Members were around at that time in this Chamber, but I think there were quite a lot of complaints about traffic and other disamenities caused.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, it was a "push" factor when STC was relocated from Bukit Timah.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There was a letter, I think, that came in 1998, where a resident wrote in to the Forum Page to say, "The traffic situation has worsened along Dunearn Road on race days, specifically between the Turf Club entrance and Clementi Road junction.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The heavy vehicle flow is impeded by turnings into Swiss Club Road and the best solution for the Turf Club is move to another site, away from the residential zone, as reported in The Straits Times some time ago.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I hope that Bukit Turf Club committee is seriously searching for an alternative site." And then, it goes on to make a lot more complaints about the traffic situation and it was signed off as "Long-suffering Citizen".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And questions were also raised in Parliament at that time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr S Dhanabalan, who was the Minister for National Development, mentioned that they would have to think about relocating Turf Club.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Dr Richard Hu, who was the Finance Minister at that time, also made the same point.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The other issue that came up was whether or not the Bukit Timah Turf Club site was best used for horse racing, given that it was prime land.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And questions were raised in Parliament about that as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the approach back in 1998/1999 was that Bukit Timah Turf Club was moved out of Bukit Timah because of the disamenities that it was causing and because that was not the best use for that land, and it was given the Kranji site in replacement.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But at that time, what we did was we earmarked it as land reserved for housing, but not for immediate development.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, that is why it was reflected in the 1998 Master Plan as for housing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think now, as our housing programme picks up pace, we will be looking at developing it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But before you do that, you have to do infrastructure and road networks.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You cannot just build a housing development there and then not have all the surrounding infrastructure, services, amenities and so on.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As Members would know, one of the Mass Rapid Transit stations, which has just been announced, would be at that site.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: We have been on this topic for quite a while.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If I may just build off the question by Member Joan Pereira about stakeholder consultations and, in light of press reports that indicate that many stakeholders expressed surprise and dismay at the decision, I am wondering if the Ministers are willing to share if a formal stakeholder consultation process will now be undertaken with residents in the neighbourhood with regard to future plans for this Turf Club site and, more generally, if the notion of a stakeholder consultation process for any major Government decision with public policy implications will be weaved into more standard practice.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The answer to the first one is yes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is an ongoing conversation because as Members can imagine, when the announcement was first made, many were, shall we say, it came out of the blue.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, it is taking some time to adjust to the announcement and obviously with the employees as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With respect to the surrounding area, there are not a lot of residential dwellings in the immediate vicinity.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But it is part of the Housing and Development Board's normal consultations when they ask people, "What would you like for your town or for your area?" So, that will take place.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the second part, I think Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked when we would consult.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think we have been doing a lot of that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, Acts, Bills, some of them, in fact, the majority of them are put out for public consultation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When we have the Remaking Our Heartlands exercise, for example, that is put out for public engagement, consultation ideas and suggestions.
